Topic T1 · First Impression

Where You'd Find It
The physical box: pocket D2 is column D (fourth from the left), second row up from the edge furthest from the lid hinge. It holds two black fender washers.

What You'd Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item D2 is a thin, black steel washer whose outside diameter is about three times its hole. Two features stand out before you read a word: the oversized rim, and a black finish with a hint of olive-gold showing through on some pieces. Take a few moments to review and examine the part.

As received: black fender washers on a grid, one on edge to show the 1.6 mm thickness. Each grid square is 5 mm — an 18 mm washer spans a little over three and a half squares, and fits just inside the 20 mm square on the size card.
The E-Catalog’s 3D model: a plain flat ring. Everything about its shape comes down to three numbers — outside diameter, inside diameter and thickness.

Black Dye Finish — the black color is a dye applied over olive-green zinc plating. The “BD” in OGBD.

Fender Proportions — 18 mm across with a 6.4 mm hole — the rim is about three times the M6 bolt it serves. That oversized rim is what makes it a fender washer.

Olive Undertone — where the dye is thin, the olive-green chromate underneath shows through as a gold, iridescent sheen. The “OG” in OGBD.

Washer on Edge — standing on its edge against the size card, the washer shows its 1.6 mm thickness — about a third of one 5 mm grid square.

Topic T3 · Fender Washers & DIN 9021

A Large-Size Washer, Built to DIN 9021

The description calls this an M6 fender washer, DIN 9021, grade A. Here is what each of those words tells you — and the table every dimension comes from.

What Is a Fender Washer?

Large OD, Small Hole

SBS defines fender washers as flat washers with a larger outer diameter in proportion to the center hole. This one: an 18 mm rim around a 6.4 mm hole.

Why the Big Rim

The wide face spreads the clamping load over a larger area — useful on thin sheet metal, plastic, or oversized and slotted holes, where a standard washer would pull through.

Sized by the Bolt

A washer is named for the bolt it fits, not its own dimensions. “M6” means it is made for an M6 bolt — the hole is a little larger, at 6.4 mm.

The Fender Washers category, with SBS’s definition at the top (click to enlarge).
The DIN 9021 Standard
DIN 9021 (1990), page 1. Our row — nominal size 6,4 for an M6 thread — is outlined. Open DIN 9021 (1990) ↗

Scope

DIN 9021 covers large size washers in product grades A and C, with an outside diameter of about three times the nominal thread diameter, for hexagon head bolts and nuts.

The M6 Row

Hole d1: 6.4–6.62 mm. Outside diameter d2: 17.57–18 mm. Thickness h: 1.6 mm nominal, 1.4–1.8 mm. These are the limits on the inspection report (T7).

Read the Commas

The standard uses a decimal comma, as ISO documents do: 6,4 means 6.4 mm and 17,57 means 17.57 mm.

Grade & Weight

Grade A

DIN 9021 has two product grades. The description calls for grade A — the finer grade, as opposed to the coarser grade C.

A Quick Weight Check

DIN 9021 gives about 2.79 kg per 1,000 washers for size 6,4 — roughly 2.8 g each, which the E-Catalog rounds up to 0.01 lb.

Topic T4 · Steel & Zinc Plating

Steel, Zinc Plated

No material letter appears in .6NMFA-OGBD/PR, and the E-Catalog confirms it: this washer is plain steel. Steel rusts, so the part depends on its plating to survive — which is why the finish gets so much attention on this item.

Requirement

Material: Steel · Plating: electrodeposited zinc, Fe/Zn 8 · Over the zinc: olive-green chromate and black dye

Reading the Material

When a part number or description does not state a material, the reasonable assumption is plain steel — about 90% of global fasteners. If the part were stainless, you would expect an “S” in the number.

Why Plated Steel

Plated steel costs a fraction of stainless — stainless typically runs two to four times more — so a plating that holds up is the economical way to protect a washer.

Reading “Fe/Zn 8”

Fe

The base metal: iron, meaning steel.

Zn

The coating: zinc, electrodeposited (electroplated) onto the part.

8

The minimum zinc thickness: 8 µm (micrometres).

D

In ASTM F1941’s designation Fe/Zn 8D, the letter is the supplementary finish — D is the olive-green chromate.

Two Standards, One Coating

ASTM B633 on the Print

The BRP print calls out ASTM B633-07, Fe/Zn 8, Type II, olive green: the general standard for electrodeposited zinc on iron and steel. Type II means a colored chromate conversion coating.

ASTM F1941M in the Description

The SBS extended description cites ASTM F1941M-07 Fe/Zn 8D: the specification for electrodeposited coatings on mechanical fasteners. Same 8 µm of zinc, same olive chromate.

Which One Governs?

On a per-print part the customer print is the controlling document. When a print and a description cite different standards, raise it with Quality rather than picking one yourself.

Salt Spray: Where Plating Is Proven

White Rust

White corrosion products mean the zinc is corroding — the coating doing its sacrificial job, but sooner than it should.

Red Rust

Red rust means the zinc has been used up and the steel itself is corroding. On a plated part, early red rust is a failure.

This Item’s History

NCR C19-3587VA (March 2019): parts showed premature white and red rust during salt spray testing. See for the full history.

Topic T5 · Olive Green Black Dye

Olive Green, Then Black

“-OGBD” at the end of the part number names the finish: Olive Green Black Dye. Two layers of color sit on top of the zinc, and the inspection report shows exactly what an acceptable part looks like.

Requirement

FINISH TYPE 2 — RECOUVREMENT DE ZINC ÉLECTROLYTIQUE ET COLORANT NOIR / ASTM B633-07, Fe/Zn8, TYPE II OLIVE GREEN, ELECTRODEPOSITED ZINC COATING AND BLACK DYE.From BRP print 589032581. The print is bilingual — French first, then English.

OG — Olive Green

An olive-green chromate conversion coating over the zinc. It adds corrosion resistance on top of what the zinc alone provides.

BD — Black Dye

A black dye over the olive chromate turns the part black for appearance.

Why It Can Look Gold

Where the dye is thin, the olive chromate shows through as a gold-green, iridescent sheen — look for it on the sample washers.

OK vs. NOK: The Visual Aid
The visual aid on the inspection report: NOK on the left, OK on the right.

NOK — Bright Silver

A bright, uncolored zinc washer. The olive chromate and black dye are missing, so the part does not meet the print.

OK — Uniform Black

An even black finish over the whole washer, both faces and the edges.

The SBS Finish Guide
The SBS Finish Guide entry for Olive Green with Black Dye, beside Clear Zinc Nickel (click to enlarge). Coatings and Finishes | Specialty Bolt & Screw Inc. ↗

Not Preferred

The Finish Guide flags this finish as not preferred due to quality issues — the same story the four NCRs tell.

Better Options

For a black finish, the guide suggests Black Zinc or Black Zinc Nickel instead. On a per-print part, any change has to go through the customer first.

HE Risk

The card carries an HE Risk (hydrogen embrittlement) badge, as electroplated zinc finishes do. It matters most on high-strength fasteners.

Finish Type 1 vs. Type 2

Not to Be Confused With Finish Type 1

The same print defines finish type 1 for the other washer it controls: zinc-nickel with a black sealer, ASTM F1941M-07 Fe/Zn-Ni 8ET/F, with a glossy black appearance. Our washer is type 2.

Topic T6 · Per Print Parts

Defined by a Drawing That Calls Up a Standard

The “/PR” in the part number means per print. This item shows how lean a print can be: BRP’s drawing adds a part number and a finish to a washer that DIN 9021 already defines.

What “Per Print” Means

The part is defined by either a customer or supplier drawing. It is not a standard or catalog part.

Standard Shape, Customer Finish

The geometry is pure DIN 9021. The olive green black dye finish and the BRP part number are what make it a customer part.

Why It Isn’t Off the Shelf

DIN 9021 washers are common, but not in this finish. The description alone cannot define it — you need the print.

Document Controlled

All per-print parts are document controlled in P21, with the print linked to the item.

Opening the Print in P21

Document Links Tab

In Item Maintenance or Item Master Inquiry, open the Document Links tab. Right-click the print link to open it.

Two Active Links

The BRP print, 589032581, and the INSPECTION TEMPLATE (T7). Only the print link is checked for Outside Use.

Item Maintenance → Document Links.
The BRP Arrangement Print
BRP print 589032581, Arrangement de rondelle / Washer arrangement (click to enlarge).

An Arrangement Print

Like a family print, it controls more than one part. A table at top left lists each washer; the drawing shows only the nominal diameter.

Finding Our Part

BRP part 250200164 is the second row: nominal diameter 6.4, for M6 bolts, DIN 9021, flat washer, finish type 2.

The Other Row

250200163 is an M24 washer to DIN 6916 in finish type 1 — a different washer on the same sheet.

Zoomed in: our part, 250200164, is the second row — 6.4 nominal, for M6 bolts, DIN 9021, finish type 2.
The finish notes: type 1 zinc-nickel with black sealer, and our type 2 — zinc, olive green, black dye.

The Note

“Dessin d’arrangement réservé seulement pour les rondelles qui respectent les normes DIN et ISO” — this arrangement drawing is only for washers that meet DIN and ISO standards. The standard supplies every dimension.

Read the Title Block

Metric, not to scale. The material field says VOIR TABLEAU / SEE TABLE — and the table points to the DIN standard.

Revisions & Deviations

Revision A

Drawn in September 2015. Revision A (2015-10-01) added P/N 250200164 — our washer. It matches the REV A in the extended description and on the inspection report.

Préliminaire

The word PRÉLIMINAIRE (preliminary) sits beside the table. If you quote or source from this print, confirm its status with the customer.

When a New Revision Arrives

Find out whether SBS has inventory worldwide or parts on order with a supplier. A print change may make that material non-conforming.

Deviation

In that case we negotiate with the customer to use the parts made to the old revision under a deviation.

Quick Reference: The Decoded Part Number

Keep this in mind — the same breakdown from Topic T2, all in one place.

.6NMFA-OGBD/PR
  • .Metric. The leading period marks this as a metric part.
  • 6Bolt Size. M6 — the bolt this washer fits, not its own size.
  • NNo Thread. A no-thread product — the washer has no thread of its own.
  • MFAFender Washer. The SBS short code for a fender washer, here to DIN 9021.
  • -OGBDFinish. Olive Green Black Dye over zinc plating.
  • /PRPer Print. Defined by a customer drawing — BRP 589032581.

1. In .6NMFA-OGBD/PR, what does the “6” represent?

Correct — washers are named for the bolt they fit. This one fits an M6 bolt.

Not quite — the 6 is the M6 bolt size; the washer itself is 18 mm across with a 6.4 mm hole.

2. What does “OGBD” stand for?

Correct — an olive-green chromate over zinc, finished with a black dye.

Not quite — OGBD is Olive Green Black Dye, the finish.

3. Per DIN 9021, a large size (fender) washer’s outside diameter is roughly…

Correct — about 3× the thread: 18 mm for M6.

Not quite — DIN 9021 sets the OD at roughly three times the nominal thread diameter.

4. On the inspection report, what are the limits for outside diameter d2?

Correct — straight from DIN 9021 Table 1, size 6,4.

Not quite — d2 is 17.57 min to 18.00 max, from DIN 9021 Table 1.

5. Why does BRP print 589032581 list two different part numbers?

Correct — one print, two washers: 250200163 (M24, DIN 6916) and our 250200164.

Not quite — it is an arrangement print controlling two washers.

Reference

Glossary

Every code and term used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term's "jump" button to see it in context.

AQL

Acceptable Quality Level — the sampling basis for accepting or rejecting a lot. This item’s inspection report uses a 2% AQL.

Arrangement Print

A customer drawing that controls several similar parts through a table, like a family print. BRP print 589032581 controls two washers.

ASTM B633

The standard for electrodeposited zinc coatings on iron and steel. Called out on the BRP print as Fe/Zn 8, Type II olive green.

ASTM F1941

The specification for electrodeposited coatings on mechanical fasteners. Cited in the SBS extended description as Fe/Zn 8D.

BRP

Bombardier Recreational Products — the customer whose print controls this part. Only users logged in with SBS or BRP credentials can see the part on the E-Catalog.

Chromate Conversion Coating

A thin chemical film formed on zinc plating that adds corrosion resistance and color. On this part it is olive green.

DIN 9021

The German standard for large size washers, grades A and C, with an outside diameter about three times the nominal thread diameter.

Fe/Zn 8

Zinc (Zn) electroplated on iron or steel (Fe) at a minimum thickness of 8 µm.

Fender Washer

A flat washer with a large outside diameter in proportion to its center hole, used to spread clamp load over a wider area.

Grade A

The finer of the two product grades in DIN 9021, called out in this item’s description. Grade C is the coarser grade.

HE Risk

Hydrogen embrittlement risk — electroplating can introduce hydrogen that makes high-strength steel brittle. The SBS Finish Guide flags it on each finish.

NCR

Non-conformance report — a record of parts that did not meet requirements. All four NCRs on this item concern the finish.

OGBD

Olive Green Black Dye — an olive chromate over zinc plating, finished with a black dye. The “-OGBD” in the part number.

Per Print (/PR)

A part defined by a customer or supplier drawing rather than a standard or catalog design. It cannot be defined by words alone.

PPAP Level 4

A Production Part Approval Process submission whose contents are defined by the customer. Shown in the header of this item’s inspection report.

White Rust / Red Rust

White corrosion means the zinc coating is corroding; red rust means the steel underneath is. Both showed up early in this item’s 2019 salt spray NCR.
